The computer turns on but nothing appears on the monitor. Also called black screen / blank screen.
Check monitor and system power LEDs.
Check both ends of the display cable (VGA/HDMI/DP).
Test the monitor/cable with another known-working device if available.
If internal inspection is needed, ask your teacher or a qualified technician.
Programs take a long time to open or the system feels sluggish.
Close unused programs and browser tabs.
Open Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc) and check high CPU/Memory/Disk usage.
Remove temporary files and check free storage.
Disable unnecessary startup apps (Task Manager → Startup).
The computer cannot connect to a wireless network.
Network adapter disabled or driver issue
Make sure Wi-Fi is on and Airplane mode is off.
Select the correct network and re-enter the password carefully.
Restart the computer and, if allowed, the router.
Check if another device can connect to the same Wi-Fi.
If only this PC fails, check adapter settings or ask your teacher.
A printer is connected but documents do not print.
Make sure the printer is on and error-free.
Check paper, ink/toner, and cable/Wi-Fi connection.
Confirm the correct printer is selected in the app.
Cancel stuck jobs in the print queue if needed.
Print a test page; ask for help if it still fails.
The computer is running but there is no audio.
Select the correct output device (Settings → Sound).
Reconnect headset/speaker and test another port.
Test another app or audio file.
If it remains, check Device Manager or ask for assistance.
A program does not launch or closes immediately.
Close the app fully (Task Manager if needed) and try again.
Use approved repair/reinstall or ask your teacher.
Some or all keyboard keys do not respond.
For wireless: check battery and USB receiver.
Restart; test another known-working keyboard if available.
The connection works but pages and downloads are very slow.
Move closer to the access point.
Close heavy downloads/streams on this and nearby devices.
Check if other devices are also slow.
If the whole network is slow, report to the teacher/admin.
The computer becomes unusually hot or the fan runs loudly.
Save work and close unnecessary programs.
Place the device on a hard, flat surface.
Ensure vents are not blocked (avoid beds/sofas).
Let it cool before heavy tasks.
If overheating continues, ask a qualified technician.
The drive has very little free space left.
Remove temporary files using system tools (Disk Cleanup/Storage Sense).
Move or delete files only after confirming they are not needed.
Pressing the power button does nothing — no lights, no fan.
Loose power cable or outlet issue
Check the power cable at both ends (wall and PC).
Ensure the power strip/UPS and wall switch are on.
Try another outlet you know works.
Look for any power LED or fan spin; note what you see.
If still dead, do not open the PSU — ask a technician.
Windows shows a blue screen with an error code and restarts.
Note the stop code (e.g., 0x...). Take a clear photo.
Restart and see if it happens again.
Undo the last change (new driver/hardware) if possible.
If it repeats, report the code to your teacher/technician.
The cursor does not move or clicks don't register.
Reconnect the mouse / re-seat the receiver.
Clean the sensor and try a mousepad.
Test another mouse to isolate the fault.
Many pop-ups, redirects, or unknown programs appear.
Do not click pop-ups; close the browser.
Run a scan with Windows Security (or approved antivirus).
Ask your teacher before installing any cleaner tool.
“USB device not recognized” appears when plugging something in.
Unplug and replug firmly; try another port.
Try the device on another computer.
In Device Manager, scan for hardware changes.
If it still fails, the device may be faulty.
Wi-Fi shows connected but no website loads.
Try another website and another browser.
Restart the PC; if allowed, restart the router.
If all devices are affected, report to admin.
The computer takes a very long time to reach the desktop.
Check Startup apps (Task Manager → Startup) and disable unneeded ones.
Ask your teacher about storage upgrade options.
The screen flickers or shows random lines.
Turn off the monitor and PC before reseating the display cable.
Set the recommended resolution and refresh rate in Display Settings.
If the issue began after a driver update, ask your teacher before updating or rolling back the display driver.
Test with another known-working monitor or cable if available.
If flickering continues, stop and ask a qualified technician.
Others cannot hear you or you cannot hear them.
Unmute and raise mic volume; test in Sound → Input.
Reconnect the headset; try another port.
Test the headset on another device.
Updates download or install for a very long time or fail.
Ensure stable internet and enough storage.
Restart only if Windows is not actively installing an update.
Run the Windows Update troubleshooter if it is available.
If a download is stuck, pause and resume it; if installation is stuck, allow more time.
Do not force shutdown during “Do not turn off” — wait or ask for help.
The battery percentage drops quickly even with light use.
Battery health has declined with age or wear
Lower brightness; set Power mode to Balanced/Battery Saver.
Close unused apps and browser tabs.
If health is very low, ask a technician about replacement.
The system keeps asking for the Wi-Fi password even when correct.
Restart the PC and router if allowed.
Check if other devices connect with the same password.
Ask admin if MAC filtering is enabled.
